QuoteIQ’s model caps at $699/month for unlimited users regardless of how many pools you service, so route growth never changes what you pay. Both models are legitimate; they just distribute risk differently between the vendor and the operator. Is there a cheaper alternative to Skimmer? + For most working route sizes, yes. QuoteIQ runs 79–85% cheaper from roughly 100 serviced locations upward because it bills per user instead of per pool: 100 pools is $200/month on Skimmer versus $29.99 on QuoteIQ Essentials; 400 pools is $800 versus $149.99 on Pro; 1,000 pools is $2,000 versus $299 on Elite. Skimmer’s line passes QuoteIQ Max at $699 with unlimited users at about 350 locations and keeps climbing. Two honest exceptions: at very small route sizes with large crews Skimmer is cheaper, since a 3-person team on 49 pools pays $49/month on Skimmer versus $149.99 on QuoteIQ Pro; and seasonal northern operators who close pools for winter aren’t billed for those months, so their real annual cost is lower than a straight twelve-month multiplication. QuoteIQ also includes the AI receptionist that Skimmer sells at $99/month, plus unlimited photos against Skimmer’s per-visit caps. Does Skimmer have AI? + Yes, and it’s good — anyone telling you otherwise is misinformed. Skimmer AI Phone is a 24/7 AI phone agent trained on pool-specific language, chemistry, and equipment. It answers from a knowledge base built from your website, captures leads straight into Skimmer with customer details and notes, recognizes existing customers, routes urgent calls to a human under configurable rules, and includes a toggle controlling whether it identifies itself as AI. The differences are price and breadth. Skimmer AI Phone costs $99/month on top of your subscription on every tier; QuoteIQ Virtual Call Team is included on every plan from $29.99. And QuoteIQ ships four additional AI products Skimmer doesn’t offer at any price: AI Estimator for photo-to-quote generation, Before/After AI for marketing images, AI Autopilot for natural-language CRM control, and AI Text Generator. On the receptionist specifically, the capability gap is small — the $1,188/year cost gap is not. What’s included in Skimmer’s $49 plan? + Skimmer’s Getting Started tier starts at $49/month covering 49 serviced locations, and it includes unlimited technicians and admins, unlimited customers and service locations, the Route Builder, one-time work orders, invoicing, online payments, financial reporting, the customer portal, service reports and emails, surcharging, and real-time QuickBooks Online sync. What it does not include, per their own feature matrix , is substantial: no Quotes and Estimates, no Job Management, no Schedule, no Recurring Work Order Schedules, no Route Optimizer, no LSI and Dosing Calculator, no LaMotte integration, no Productivity Reports, no Broadcast Emails, no Sunbit financing, and no live phone support. Service texts are metered at $0.029 per message and photos are capped at 5 per visit and 20 per location. A pool pro who wants to send a quote or optimize a route needs the $98 Scaling Up tier, so that is realistically the entry price. QuoteIQ Essentials at $29.99 includes the full estimate builder, scheduling , invoicing , and the complete AI suite with no feature amputation. Does QuoteIQ track pool chemistry readings? + Partially, and it’s worth being precise because this is where Skimmer is genuinely stronger. QuoteIQ can record chemistry readings through QuoteIQ Cam’s custom Inspection Forms (Beginner $74.99 and above), which let you build reusable templates with whatever fields your techs need — free chlorine, combined chlorine, pH, total alkalinity, calcium hardness, cyanuric acid, salt, temperature — captured on mobile alongside timestamped photos, then saved into the Customer History Documentation Archive on each client contact and viewable by customers through the client portal . What QuoteIQ does not do is calculate the Langelier Saturation Index, generate dosing recommendations, flag out-of-range values automatically, or sync readings from a LaMotte Spin Touch. Skimmer does all four through its Orenda integration. If your operating model is chemistry-first and you rely on automated LSI balance and dose calculation, Skimmer is the better technical fit and this page won’t argue otherwise. If your techs already know their dosing and you mainly need the readings logged, timestamped, archived, and shown to the customer, QuoteIQ covers that at a fraction of the per-pool cost. Can I use one software for pool service and pressure washing? + With QuoteIQ, yes. With Skimmer, no — it is pool and spa only, by design and without apology, and a pool company that adds a second service line runs a second system or leaves. QuoteIQ covers 50+ trades on the same account , including pool service , pressure washing , deck restoration, screen enclosure cleaning, and general property maintenance — without switching platforms, retraining crews, or reimporting your customer list. That combination is common in pool service because the customer overlap is nearly total: the homeowner paying for weekly pool service also has a pool deck, a screen cage, a driveway, and a roof. MapMeasure Pro measures deck and hardscape square footage from satellite for exactly this kind of add-on quoting, AI Estimator builds the quote from a photo, and Pipelines & Deals tracks the larger repair and renovation jobs through multi-stage approval. Per the U.S. Small Business Administration , raising revenue per existing customer is generally cheaper than acquiring new ones. Skimmer is an excellent piece of software and the right answer for a real set of pool businesses — chemistry-first operations, small routes with big crews, hard-seasonal northern markets. The question this page exists to answer is narrower: if your pool count is climbing and your software bill is climbing with it, what does that cost over the next three years?
